title: Guardian Knight
paragraphs: “Eclair seems to be having a tough time, too… Can’t we send him off using Motoyasu’s portal or something?”
“That’s not possible.”

You can’t use the portal skill to travel with anyone who isn’t a party member. It’s impossible for that Trash to join our party, and we can’t enslave him either. Since he’s technically an imposter, we can’t send him off.
“It looks convenient, but the downside is that there are some drawbacks, huh?”
“I wonder if they’ll confiscate the plane we used to escort Itsuki?”
“That seems likely, but I’m not sure. It looks pretty hard to fly, though… Besides, a plane isn’t the only way to transport someone by air. There might be various ways to handle it.”
After we talked about that, Father smiled. Father in this world is as kind as ever.
“Well then, let’s do our best from here on out, Motoyasu-kun. You’ll get to see Yuki-chan and Kou again.”

I guess the reason he didn’t call out Sakura-chan is because Filo-tan is Sakura-chan? Unfortunately, I spent quite a bit of time with Yuki-chan and the others. Well, either way, we should be happy about the reunion.
After all, I met Yuki-chan under a different name during the last loop. In that sense, Filo-tan is the same as Sakura-chan.

As for Kou… I’ll have to be careful not to make Father angry. He’s usually well-behaved when Big Sister and her friends are around… but they’re not here right now. The only other time is when Father is in a bad mood. I’ll need to be on my guard.
So, after Father and I finished talking, I went over to greet Yuki-chan and the others, who were waiting there.
“Ah, Naofumi, welcome back.”
“I’m back.”
Oh… it’s Sakura-chan. And what’s more, she has eyes the same color as her hair—something particularly rare even within these loops. Uuuh… Sakura-chan, why aren’t you Filo-chan? Waaaaaah!
“Motoyasu-sama!”
Yuki-chan called out to me, so I snapped back to reality. I’m sure I have a sharp, determined look on my face right now. Sharp!
“Oh, Yuki-chan, how are you doing?”
“We really did a great job, didn’t we?”
…That’s right. With Yuki-chan and the others, there’s no doubt we did a great job.
“Of course! Between the despicable Schiltfreiden and the fake Melromarc Army, we handled them all with ease thanks to everyone’s strength.”
“That’s right! Now, everyone, it’s time to revel in the sweet wine of victory! Let’s just be happy about it.”

At Yuki-chan’s call, Lady Filolial and the others all raised their voices in unison. Hehehe… what a heartwarming sight. I’d love to keep watching this scene forever, with Feero-tan right here with us. And so, our war with Siltfreiden came to an end, and we held a banquet at the castle.
“Honestly… for the people of that country to confuse freedom with tradition and turn their fangs on their own homeland…”

Sighs like these could be heard all around the banquet hall. Well, after all, Shieldfreeden is a country with a short history, founded by immigrants from Siltvelt. I suppose they’re viewed as a nation that hasn’t truly stood on its own two feet yet.

And yet, they got carried away and started a war based on false accusations. I suppose it feels like being bitten by a child. So, amidst this atmosphere, the people of Siltvelt are holding discussions—interwoven with the banquet—about how to punish Shieldfreeden, making for a rather unusual gathering.
“This feels kind of gloomy.”
Father has sensed this mood as well and is scanning the room.
“Huh? I hear some lively voices coming from over there.”
Lively chatter could be heard from a corner of the banquet hall. Father beckons us over as he heads toward the commotion.
“Come on, down it in one! Down it in one!”
“Whoa! That’s good!”

It seems that’s where the mercenaries who had distinguished themselves on the battlefield were making a racket at the banquet. There’s a commotion going on—you could even call it a riot. There’s quite a contrast in atmosphere compared to the nobles’ side.
“Go for it! Big Sis!”
“Show them what you’re made of, Big Sis!”
I feel like I’ve heard those cheers before. Father, who had been watching the group from a distance, ran over to me and, with eyes sparkling like a child’s, pointed at them.
“Motoyasu! A panda! There’s a panda! And it’s drinking and having a great time!”
Hmm… A panda, you say? Looking in the direction Father was pointing—looking so delighted—there was indeed a panda. It was the very same panda that used to play with my Older Sisters all the time.
“That’s amazing. I knew there were all kinds of Demi-Human beasts out there, but so it turns out there are pandas too.”
“Indeed. By the way, there was a world where he and Father got along quite well.”
“Huh? Really?”
“That’s right. Father used to pay him a lot of attention.”

Along with Older Sister’s older sisters, mind you. After peace was restored, he even hung out with Keel. By the way, according to Luna-chan’s assessment, he was classified as “cute despite his large build.” You know… I think he was going for that “creepy-cute” vibe that really showed off Father’s taste. Though personally, I didn’t find the panda in a tutu particularly cute. Just as we were talking about this, an old man of the Gemu race came over to us.
“Oh my, what’s the matter?”
“Well, I was just watching and thinking there were some people really livening up the party.”
Saying that, Father was staring intently at the panda.
“Ah, those are the mercenaries who participated in this battle. They’re the ones who achieved great feats in a different arena from the Heroes.”
“In that case, we’ll have to make sure to reward them properly.”
“Of course. I imagine there will be an opportunity later for the Shield Hero himself to offer words of praise. So, Shield Hero, are you curious about that mercenary?”
“Huh? Well, yeah. How should I put it? In my world, they’re considered exotic beasts—or rather, very popular animals. I just thought, ‘So there really are Therianthropes like that…’”
“Hmm, hmm.”

I thought I saw a gleam in the old man of the Genmu clan’s eyes, but maybe it was just my imagination? Could he still be plotting to arrange a marriage? My memory’s a bit fuzzy, but I’m pretty sure I turned him down in this world, too.
“Anyway, rather than sitting here exchanging nothing but gloomy complaints, I think it’d be better for us to join those people over there celebrating their victory and enjoy the festivities.”
Seeing Father like that, the old man of the Genmu race nodded with a smile.
“That’s right. If we don’t enjoy the moment, we’ll never make it through the battles ahead. Heroes, please enjoy yourselves to the fullest.”
“If we want to liven things up, wouldn’t it boost morale if Father served up some food?”

I’m pretty sure his cooking—especially the Éclairs—was a big hit with Éclair and the others on our way to Siltvelt. What’s more, I’ve eaten Father’s cooking countless times across the loops. In every single instance, there were no words to describe it other than ‘delicious.’
“Huh? Am I supposed to cook and serve food for that many people? It wouldn’t be impossible if I had help, but would my cooking really boost morale that much?”
“That’s not really a method I’d recommend. The dishes prepared by the Shield Hero are like divine fare… It’s easy to imagine the nobles swarming around them, desperate to get their hands on them.”
“It might turn into a rather cutthroat banquet in a different sense… Politics really is tough, isn’t it?”
“Shield Hero, our greatest joy is for you to enjoy this banquet without worrying too much about us.”

So seeing Father enjoying himself is what brings joy to the people of Siltvelt. That’s quite a noble way of thinking. I must say, he truly lives up to his reputation as an elder of the Genmu clan. He certainly lives up to his age.
“Understood. Well then, I suppose I’ll join in so everyone can enjoy themselves without feeling self-conscious.”
After Father spoke in a cheerful voice, he blended into the lively crowd with remarkable nonchalance. Do the therianthropes around him not even notice? This is truly a mystery.
Well, Sakura-chan, Kou, and Lady Filolial are all eating nearby, drawn in by the lively atmosphere. Everyone’s just going with the flow, so they’ve probably forgotten that Father is the Shield Hero.
“Ikki! Ikki! Ooh!”
The feast went on in that sort of spirit.
The next day… Just as the old man of the Genmu clan had testified, an audience with Father was held as a reward for the mercenaries who had distinguished themselves on the battlefield.
“Well… You fought well for the country in this battle. I will grant you a reward befitting your service. Thank you. I hope you’ll continue to lend your strength to the country in the future.”
With the leading figures of Siltvelt standing by, Father thanked the mercenaries one by one. It seemed like he was just going through the motions, saying exactly what he was told to say.

The mercenaries’ reactions varied widely. Some were tense, some were relaxed, and some saluted earnestly. There were plenty who, making it look as if they were suddenly reaching out to Father, raised their swords instead.

Father didn’t flinch at all in response to the sword-raising gesture, which bordered on provocation. He was likely already assessing them based on their level and stats. When he responded, he was met with a whistle and a reply asking for continued cooperation. As expected, this is one of those unique rules of Siltvelt where strength is everything.
Soon after… Panda arrived with his pack of werewolves. He seems to be wearing a face that’s somewhere between a scowl and a blush—almost like he’s joking.
“Ah!”
By the way, at the banquet the day before, the Panda had challenged Father to a drinking contest, which had the whole venue in an uproar—only to end up completely passed out from drunkenness.
“You…”

Is he still holding a grudge about being humiliated at the banquet? Father is raising his hands, looking like he’s saying, “Sorry, sorry.” Then, after hearing from his subordinates about the reward for Panda, Father furrowed his brow. Perhaps losing patience, a Shusaku man and a Genmu elder—acting as his aides—spoke up together.

“To Rasa-zusa, a mercenary who fought with the prowess of a thousand men, we bestow the title of Guardian Knight of the Shield Hero as a reward for his recent exploits. We hope that, with his strength, he will protect the Shield Hero from any crisis and serve as his pillar of strength.”
As if to say he hadn’t heard a word of it, Father glared at the two of them, but they both wore expressions that suggested they’d acted thoughtfully.
“Ooooooh…”
Those around them could only let out cries of surprise at the magnitude of the reward. It felt as if they were being told to follow in Panda’s footsteps in the next battle, didn’t it?

And so, with the reward ceremony for the mercenaries over, the number of people in the throne room dropped sharply. Then, after confirming that the crowd had thinned out, Father looked at the representatives from Siltvelt with a slightly displeased expression.
“…What’s the reward for Ms. Rasazusa? My personal guard, perhaps?”

“Given that the Shield Hero is expected to continue leveling up and carrying out activities in various regions, we must deploy capable personnel to support him. Otherwise, we’d lose face as citizens of Siltvelt.”

“She made a good impression at the banquet the other day, and I’ve heard she fought like a war god on the battlefield. Furthermore, given her status as a mercenary, we’ve determined she’s a suitable match for the Hero, who dislikes arranged marriages.”
“Does she want this herself?”
“You’re welcome to ask her that yourself.”
Right after that exchange, Panda was summoned again and came over.
“Huh? What do you want now?”
“Yeah. I just want to ask—I heard I’ve been appointed as your Guardian Knight. Is that okay with you?”
“Ah… well, I guess. I’m a mercenary anyway, and the pay itself is exceptional. I took the job because I figured it was a good deal.”
“I see… Well, if that’s the case, then it’s fine.”
At that point, Father looked at Panda and the representative with a suspicious gaze.
“Are you really not up to anything?”
I get the feeling Panda’s back straightened slightly. Perhaps sensing this, Father’s suspicious gaze doesn’t waver.

“It’s only natural to be suspicious. Well… if I had to say something, let’s just say we’re hoping for some compensation when, after sharing both hardships and joys, the Shield Hero graces this Guardian Knight with his heart…”
“We’re just assigning him as a comrade for now, but we’re hoping something more might come of it?”
Father narrows his eyes as he looks at the panda.
“A hefty reward if you have a child.”

Whether it’s a poker face or not, the panda shows no reaction. Is it just my imagination that his lack of reaction makes him seem guilty? As always, this guy has a keen eye for money. He’s an impressive panda—in a different way than the Lazy Pig.
“I’ve heard it’s just ‘what-if’ talk, too! I’d appreciate it if you didn’t worry about it too much.”
“If you start sneaking up on me night after night dressed in some weird outfit, I’ll turn you down, okay?”
“Fine by me. I’m only in it for the reward anyway.”
“Well… maybe it’s good that she’s so straightforward and clear about things?”

And so, the panda and her pack of werewolves were hired at the castle, and before we knew it, the panda had joined our group. However… the panda ended up getting to know Father quite well through a strange twist of fate.
